items.headline: FMRB executive order classified-annex response clock
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's fourth calendar day rolls to Wednesday's fifth and the deadline tightens from T-minus-two to T-minus-one business day against the Friday May 22 expiry. Tuesday's two-of-eight witness count rises to three of eight as the Office of the Director of National Intelligence files the third substantive submission on top of Monday's NIST Director Locascio and Tuesday's CISA Director submissions, with the remaining five witnesses now confirming response drafts queued for late-Wednesday or Thursday filing inside the deadline window. Just Security observes the three-of-eight pace at the midpoint of the response cadence is on the steeper side of what the eight-witness slate had projected. The House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee's parallel joint-resolution draft converts from Tuesday's posted markup notice into a formal Wednesday-morning notice of markup with the slot firmed for the back half of next week and a staff memorandum circulated to committee members.

items.headline: Cyber-evaluation reciprocity perimeter advances to sixteen jurisdictions
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's fifteen-named-candidate count steps to sixteen on Wednesday as Brunei joins as the next adjacent-track Indo-Pacific signal, plus the originating UK and EU still alongside. OECD GENAI secretariat-reported member-state submissions on the attestation field schema move from past three-quarters to past four-fifths of the named candidate cohort as the business week's third day clears, with the plenary target stepping from T-minus-two weeks to T-minus-thirteen calendar days against the June 2-6 adoption window, and the secretariat re-circulates the Tuesday calendar item placing the schema-comment close on Friday May 29. Qatar's 270-day national-consultation window holds its second week, no third Gulf Cooperation Council member has yet signalled, and the United States recognition gap continues to hold open with the FMRB executive order — now at classified-annex day five — still the cited closure instrument.

items.headline: n8n CVE-2026-21858 exposure taper into deadline eve
items.diff_narrative: The day-nineteen Tuesday scan rolls to day-twenty Wednesday with the federal-civilian remediation deadline stepping from T-minus-two to T-minus-one business day. The weekday descent extends into the deadline-eve session: internet-exposed pre-1.121.0 instances fall from roughly 1,395 to roughly 1,180, the residual unpatched long-tail share eases from about 10 percent to about 9 percent, the US cohort eases from roughly 410 to roughly 340 and India from roughly 215 to roughly 180, and Censys exploitation telemetry holds flat at 1.7x baseline for a third consecutive weekday read — consistent with commodity-tier volume continuing to settle rather than ramp ahead of the deadline. The CISA federal-civilian operational directive that published Monday morning moves from its first to its second full operating day with federal-civilian operators reporting accelerating remediation completions and the directive's mandatory-attestation submission portal opening for Thursday-morning intake.

items.headline: MCP-server attack-surface telemetry holds above 91 percent
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's weekday cadence carries into Wednesday's business-week third day with each consecutive-day counter ticking up one. The credential-extraction median holds at 5 minutes for a ninth consecutive day (from an eighth) with the unprotected-versus-protected gap still near 67x, and Defender-for-Cloud quarantine on net-new MCP servers ticks from 49 percent to 50 percent — the first time the quarantine line has reached the half-of-net-new threshold and a tenth consecutive day of expansion (from a ninth). Cisco-Astrix identity-gateway tenancy edges from roughly 2,455 to roughly 2,490 enterprise tenants and Akamai SkyAtlas MCP-firewall from roughly 1,410 to roughly 1,430, with CrowdStrike Falcon for Agentic AI's managed-visibility composition nudging from 91 percent to 92 percent — a one-point uptick and the highest cross-vendor visibility reading the telemetry has carried — and the total exposed-server estimate easing from roughly 8,960 to roughly 8,870 as weekday provisioning continues.

items.headline: Loader-verification line composes its fully-settled four-paper reference surface
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's settled-artifact-set framing rolls to Wednesday's fully-settled reference surface with the federal civilian directive at its second operating day and the May 22 compliance window at T-minus-two calendar days. The consolidated 2605.07241 framework plus its 2605.07412 empirical companion plus the 2605.07588 training-surface extension plus Tuesday's 2605.07735 tenant-policy-attestation extension now form a fully-pinned four-document academic reference set the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment commitment can cite end-to-end. The LangChain, AutoGen, CrewAI, Haystack, and Pydantic AI maintainer cohort folds Tuesday's tenant-policy-attestation manifest in as an optional sixth verification surface alongside the existing five, and the DeepMind/Meta AI/Anthropic/Microsoft consolidated Python-and-Rust reference-implementation index now indexes the tenant-policy-attestation manifest alongside the training-surface harness.

items.headline: Cerebras CBRS analyst-day eve session holds the $185-235 band
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's follow-through session rolls to Wednesday's analyst-day eve session with the May 21 Alphabet analyst day stepping from T-minus-two to T-minus-one calendar day and the post-Monday consolidation base intact across its third consecutive trading day. The five-desk analyst spread carries unchanged into the third trading day inside the same roughly $185-to-$235 band, with Morgan Stanley's upside-scenario probability ticking from 42 percent to 43 percent, institutional-buyside cumulative net position edging from roughly 38 percent to roughly 39 percent of float as desks added small incremental long exposure, and the Saudi PIF contingent-secondary discussion moving from the second week into the back half of the 10-21 day execution window. The desk preview cohort treats Wednesday as the canonical pre-print session and flags the post-print Thursday session as the canonical inflection window for any cross-program allocation commentary or revenue-breakout disclosure-precedent reaction.

items.headline: Mag-7 print-cycle preview clears 90 percent breakout probability
items.diff_narrative: The Alphabet analyst day steps from Tuesday's T-minus-two to Wednesday's T-minus-one calendar day, and the run-up window enters its third and final session. The six-desk preview cohort nudges the Alphabet Q2 AI Services 10-Q footnote breakout probability from 89 percent to 90 percent — a further one-point uptick and the first time the cohort consensus has cleared the 90-percent threshold — with the Friday SEC Corp Fin fourth sample comment letter still the settled disclosure-precedent input and the cohort treating Wednesday's Cerebras pre-print trading session as a coincident input rather than a separate catalyst. The cohort now treats the Alphabet analyst-day script — released to selected sell-side desks under the standard pre-print briefing protocol — as the next concrete read on the precedent-conformance language. On the AI-accelerator IPO track, Tenstorrent's first-round comment-letter response advances from Tuesday's 12-business-day mark to a 13-business-day mark with the second-round comment letter now expected to land late Thursday or Friday, and the early-August public-filing target plus SambaNova's six-bookrunner roster both hold unchanged.

items.headline: Anthropic Claude Code 3.0 reaches 70 gated tenants two business days early
items.diff_narrative: Day twelve rolls to day thirteen with the second-week growth normalization deepening — published skills rise from roughly 32,800 to roughly 34,400 (+4.9 percent, a seventh consecutive sub-7-percent reading and the first sub-5-percent day of the second week), skill installs from roughly 2.86M to roughly 2.96M, and auto-quarantined Mythos-class skills from 71 to 73. The gated-tenant cohort extends Tuesday's weekday cadence: two further enterprise customers join to lift the Mythos-Preview count from 68 to 70, with both new entrants in the Continental European public-sector tier as the cohort's Tuesday Indo-Pacific additions and Monday's Continental European base layered into a consistent rotation. The verification harness's cross-tenant compositional safety check continues to hold under 55 seconds across all 70 tenants and now folds in Tuesday's tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification step alongside the training-surface checkpoint-provenance step. The Decoder notes the seventy-tenant mark was reached two business days ahead of the cohort's projected window.

items.headline: Mistral AI Workflows reaches ten central-government references with six-vendor matrix
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's ninth central-government reference (Sweden Skatteverket) rolls to Wednesday's tenth — and the first ten-reference reading the day-counter has carried — as Denmark Skattestyrelsen joins, the third fresh central-government estate selection of the business week. Paid Workflows tenancy edges from roughly 408 to roughly 415 enterprise customers and daily executions from roughly 7.5M to roughly 7.6M. The cross-orchestrator interop matrix expands from a five-vendor to a six-vendor matrix (Codex CLI plus Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Azure AI Foundry plus Vertex AI Agent Governance Center plus Amazon Bedrock Agent Registry) holding its first-week-of-June general-availability target with support now spanning the sixteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter's tenant-policy field schemas, and the conformance test suite holds green across all six vendors for a third consecutive weekday — with Tuesday's tenant-policy-attestation manifest check now confirmed running on every conformance pass.

items.headline: OpenAI per-org agent registry extends to eleventh Indo-Pacific region
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's ten-region Indo-Pacific GA footprint rolls to Wednesday's eleventh region as the Philippines joins (after Thailand on Tuesday and Malaysia on Monday), the third regional extension of the business week. GA-cohort tenancy edges from roughly 358 to roughly 364 enterprise customers, and OpenAI ships a Codex CLI v3.1.7 point release — two minor patches on top of Tuesday's v3.1.6 — adding optional client-side support for the tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification step from Tuesday's arxiv 2605.07735 extension as a paving step ahead of the early-June cross-orchestrator interop matrix GA target. The cohort reads the Philippines addition as continuing to track the now-sixteen-jurisdiction reciprocity perimeter rather than expand ahead of it, and flags the OECD plenary's T-minus-thirteen-day mark as the next inflection point for whether the footprint widens beyond the perimeter cohort.

items.headline: Unsloth wires tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification as sixth surface
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's 0.6 percent peak combined VRAM tightening on the refined Mixture-of-Experts router-only LoRA path gets a further roughly 0.4 percent peak combined VRAM reduction on the DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe on the same single-node octa-Hopper run, attributed to a router-attention bucket-fusion pass on top of Tuesday's all-reduce schedule refinement. The optional tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification step from Tuesday's arxiv 2605.07735 extension is now wired as the sixth verification surface alongside the existing five plus Monday's training-surface checkpoint-provenance step. The DeepSeek R3-Pro 38B recipe draws an eleventh Hacker News reproduction (from a tenth) — a single-RTX 5090 plus single-RTX 4090 hybrid consumer workstation completes the router-only run at roughly 5.1 percent peak combined VRAM on the refined path — and a third contributor merges the Qwen3 MoE 60B port from Tuesday's pull request as a stable contributed recipe.

items.headline: vLLM v0.11.4 stable settles into canonical reference state
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's first full operating day rolls to Wednesday's second with no escalations from the maintainer cohort. The Yotta Labs throughput gap holds near the roughly 2.0 percent of Tuesday's reading — about 19,210 tok/s on v0.11.4 stable versus about 19,580 tok/s on SGLang RadixArk v0.5.9, the tightest sustained band the benchmark has carried — with Cloudflare Infire holding L40S edge-tier parity at 1.00x into the third day post-stable. The v0.11.5 development branch now folds in the optional tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification hook from Tuesday's arxiv 2605.07735 extension alongside the Monday training-surface checkpoint-provenance hook as paving steps on top of the existing five-surface mitigation set, and the serving-stack cohort treats Wednesday as the canonical settle-state day on which the v0.11.4 stable tag plus the Monday CISA federal-civilian operational directive plus Tuesday's tenant-policy-attestation manifest paper can be cited together as a single coherent stable reference for the upstream framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment window.

items.headline: Tenstorrent Galaxy rack shipments cross 70-percent capacity threshold
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's weekday cadence carries into Wednesday with a fresh batch lifting the cumulative count from roughly 187 to roughly 198 racks against the 280-rack first-half target — about 71 percent fulfilled (up from about 67 percent, a four-point uptick and the first time the capacity-fulfillment curve has crossed the 70-percent threshold). Additions span CoreWeave and Lambda Labs in North America plus a third Asia-Pacific increment splitting between Yotta Labs India and CDS Japan plus a third European sovereign-cloud increment going to Outscale France and Atlante Cloud Italy on top of Tuesday's UpCloud Finland plus Telefonica Tech Spain and Monday's OVHcloud France plus Hetzner Online Germany. AMD's Helios plus MI450 commitment book advances from near 10.55GW to near 10.7GW with a fresh weekday sovereign-cloud commitment — the third new commitment of the business week — and the Tenstorrent confidential S-1 holds its early-August public-filing target.

items.headline: Cerebras CS-4 plus Vera Rubin plus AMD Helios sampling cadence holds
items.diff_narrative: Engineering-sample windows hold unchanged from Tuesday across all three accelerator tracks into the business week's third day. Cerebras's four-batch schedule still places first-batch engineering samples to lead customer OpenAI in mid-Q1 2027 with the second through fourth batches firmed through late Q3 2026 for the Apple, Mistral AI plus Cohere plus Stability AI, and AI21 Labs plus Reka AI plus Together AI cohorts; Nvidia's four shipped NVL576 engineering-sample batches hold their Tuesday allocations across the OpenAI, Meta, Anthropic, Apple, Mistral AI, xAI, and Microsoft Azure cohorts; and AMD's first MI450 Helios production-rack samples to SoftBank Cloud Japan and SK Telecom Cloud Korea hold their Tuesday status. The desk cohort flags the post-print Thursday session — rather than the May 21 analyst day itself — as the canonical next read on cross-program allocation.

items.headline: Tesla Optimus Gen 3 activates tenth Fremont cohort, crosses halfway threshold
items.diff_narrative: Tuesday's ninth cohort rolls to Wednesday's tenth: a fresh cohort of roughly twelve units comes online, lifting the active count from 108 to 120 of the disclosed 240-unit allocation — 50 percent reached (up from 45 percent) and crossing the halfway threshold of the disclosed allocation for the first time — with cycle-time still holding at the roughly 1.03x human-baseline envelope. The tenth cohort enters the Fremont automotive line on the same multi-station sealed parts-transfer chain that has been the standard cohort-onboarding workflow since the eighth-cohort activation, with cross-cell coordination on the ninth-cohort line continuing without incident through its second day of operation. The Stellantis Detroit (June 8) and Volkswagen Wolfsburg (June 22) activation dates hold, and Standard Bots notes that the roughly 12-unit weekday cadence would complete the disclosed 240-unit allocation inside the first half of June if the pattern holds.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics Atlas clears 144-hour milestone, runs toward 168-hour
items.diff_narrative: BMW Group's Spartanburg 30-unit Atlas pilot clears Tuesday's first North American 144-hour continuous-operation milestone and now runs toward a first North American 168-hour milestone on the under-body conveyor task with zero MTBF-impacting incidents. Volkswagen Wolfsburg's Atlas pilot edges from roughly 88 to roughly 91 units on the body-shop welding-jig material-handoff task as the third weekday shift carries Monday and Tuesday's expansion pattern. The humanoid league-table OEM-adopter roster's flagged seventh adopter — Mercedes-Benz Sindelfingen — moves from due-diligence to a signed 25-unit pilot commitment, lifting the roster to seven and giving the cohort its first new OEM signing since the prior six-roster formation. Hyundai Metaplant's Dangjin rolling-mill cycle-time improvement holds near 5.1 percent for a ninth consecutive within-band day (from an eighth), with the policy-distillation pipeline now coupling directly to the tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification step folded into Unsloth's training driver Wednesday.

items.headline: Wednesday arxiv 2605.07891 consolidation survey unifies loader-verification cluster
items.diff_narrative: A fresh Wednesday arxiv release, 2605.07891, opens the business week's third research day by adding a consolidation survey to the four-document loader-verification cluster — synthesizing the 2605.07241 consolidated framework, its 2605.07412 empirical companion, the 2605.07588 training-surface extension, and Tuesday's 2605.07735 tenant-policy-attestation extension into a single end-to-end verification graph spanning training-run checkpoint through agent-loader through tenant-policy gate. Positioned explicitly as a survey rather than a fresh model, it formalizes the composition properties of the four prior surfaces and tabulates the combined verification overhead across the five-tier composition, reporting only a marginal incremental overhead on top of the per-surface overheads. Simon Willison characterizes Wednesday as the loader-verification line reaching a settled survey state by mid-week, with the four primary papers plus the Wednesday survey now forming a unified five-document reference set the framework cohort's mid-June default-shipment commitment can cite as a single coherent end-to-end surface. The reproduction harness extends the existing DeepMind/Meta AI/Anthropic/Microsoft consolidated reference-implementation index to a single end-to-end run covering all five surfaces.
